particulars: All names, ages, dates, times, places, court names, charges, sentence lengths, compensation amount, employer and book title are omitted.

items.record: A single victim's eyewitness identification drives the case: "it is between number four and number five" before she settles on number five after a second viewing.
items.reading: absent; the reading imagines an official report written by a bureaucratic state body
items.loss: The core mechanism, an honest but mistaken eyewitness memory hardening into certainty through repeated police procedures, is missing.

items.record: The suspect was picked from mugshots because of a prior record: Cotton "had been arrested as a teenager for breaking and entering."
items.loss: The way a past record channels a person into suspicion is not recovered.

items.record: Exculpatory evidence was blocked: the other victim "positively identified subject number four" and the court "excluded the evidence on grounds that it was not relevant."
items.reading: absent; the reading describes a document made of true statements with misleading framing
items.loss: The concrete process by which a court shut out evidence pointing away from the defendant is missed.

items.record: An appeal partly corrected the error, and a retrial then made things worse: the high court "reversed the convictions and ordered a new trial," and at retrial "the second woman also identified Mr. Cotton."
items.reading: absent; the reading assumes steady drift with no intervening correction
items.loss: The back-and-forth sequence of reversal, retrial and a heavier conviction is lost.

items.record: The real perpetrator was screened out by witness denial: Poole was brought in and both women "contended that he was not their attacker," so the defense was denied.
items.loss: The ironic dynamic in which the same mistaken witnesses blocked the true suspect is not recovered.

items.record: Resolution came through forensic science requested by the defense: DNA testing "indicated that Mr. Cotton was not the source," and a database match identified Poole.
items.reading: resolution by leak, journalist or inquiry, described as "not cleanly, and not soon"
items.loss: The actual mechanism and agent of exposure, technical evidence pursued by one individual's defense, is misdescribed.

items.record: Prosecutor and defense jointly moved to dismiss, followed by a guilty plea and a pardon: "The district attorney and the defense filed a motion to dismiss all charges."
items.reading: the institution keeps producing rationalizing documents to suppress the problem
items.loss: The institution's cooperative self-correction once proof arrived is misdescribed as continued suppression.

items.record: A single individual, not a dispersed population, bore the harm: Cotton spent "more than 10 years in prison" for crimes Poole committed while Poole kept offending.
items.reading: an isolated mass of claimants or patients whose individual cases form a hidden pattern
items.loss: The affected party is misidentified: one wrongly convicted man, plus victims of a free perpetrator, rather than a diffuse public.

items.record: The accuser and the wrongly accused reconciled and became joint advocates: "They became good friends and began to travel around the country to speak about wrongful convictions."
items.reading: affected people stay isolated, resigned and without a collective
items.loss: The post-exoneration relationship that turned former adversaries into reform partners is missed.

items.record: The case produced a reform agenda: speaking about reforms "especially for eyewitness identification procedures."
items.reading: the archived document later serves as evidence of institutional knowledge
items.loss: The policy outcome, procedural reform of witness identification, is not recovered.

items.record: The exoneree rebuilt his life: he "got a job in the warehouse of LabCorp," married, had a child, bought land and received state compensation.
items.loss: The individual repair and restitution trajectory after release is lost.
